title: Removing the smoke screen of SMAX1 and SMXL2's role in seedling growth
content: Optimal timing of growth, life-stage transitions, and physiological processes is crucial for plant survival and fecundity. Plants constantly monitor their environment; the circadian clock anticipates the diurnal environmental changes, enabling optimal timing of molecular and physiological processes (Greenham and McClung 2015). Hypocotyl elongation is gated by the circadian clock restricting elongation to specific times of day, depending on day length and temperature cues (Niwa et al. 2009; Nusinow et al. 2011). In short days, hypocotyl elongation peaks at the end of night, whereas, in long days, hypocotyl elongation peaks during the end of the day. This time-of day dependent growth is governed by a complex signaling network starting with light and temperature perception.
